result.answer: No. From what Shutter could see, the approval was right when it was given. The demo bed-management system was read at 02:23:43 UTC on 1 Nov. It showed the patient on WARD-A (version 1). It had no receipt for the WARD-B transfer (08:20 UTC on 15 Oct) and no later move. Resending then would have put the patient where the PAS said. One second later, at 02:23:44 UTC, a later transfer to WARD-C (08:40 UTC) was applied. The approval no longer covered the send, so Shutter blocked it at the last check and closed the case with nothing to send. All three specialists agree on this. They differ in focus and certainty. The conformance view opens with "yes", but it means the message itself was sound. It also says the approval was not wrong. The impact view is less certain. Its effects on beds, pharmacy and porters come from rules, not from records those systems kept. Under a full-history setting (W1, not in use here), a person would have decided instead. You can't approve or resend anything through this answer.

perspectives.view: The approval was not wrong. At 02:23:43 UTC the record was at version 1 with no later move and no receipt. The WARD-C transfer arrived one second later, so the intent stopped holding.
The message was sound: it parsed against 2.5.1 and the receiver's dry run said it would apply. The receiver's record changed, not the message. The schema check covers structure only.

Sending at approval time would have updated beds, pharmacy and porters correctly. Sending now would cause wrong-ward effects. These effects are inferred from rules, not observed, so this view has medium confidence.

response.content: I've submitted the board's answer: all three specialists found the approval was right when it was given, and a later move to WARD-C one second afterwards, at 02:23:44 UTC on 1 Nov, is what stopped the resend.
